title: 49,999,950 USDT lost to address poisoning (Ethereum, 19 Dec 2025)
summary: After a 50 USDT test payment to its intended counterparty, the victim received a dust transfer from a lookalike and minutes later sent 49,999,950 USDT to the lookalike (as reported by several outlets).

public_sources.title: Crypto trader loses $50 million in address poisoning attack, offers $1 million bounty for return
public_sources.used_for: Harmful transaction, test payment, victim. Retrieved by a research subagent on 2026-10-27; values cross-checked on-chain, page not re-read by hand.

public_sources.used_for: Corroboration of mechanism and amount. Retrieved by a research subagent on 2026-10-27; values cross-checked on-chain, page not re-read by hand.

harm.description: The victim signed a USDT transfer of 49,999,950 USDT (6 decimals) to the lookalike.

evaluation.rationale: The 21,600 blocks (about 3 days) before and including the harmful block: the same round default as the WBTC case, fixed before any activity in the window was examined.

onchain_verification: Verified on 2026-10-28 via eth.drpc.org: tx 0xc0514a79...6a0f in block 24047560, signed by the victim, calls USDT; its receipt has one Transfer of 49999950000000 base units from the victim to 0xBaFF2F13638C04B10F8119760B2D2aE86b08f8b5; status success.
Verified: eth_getCode(victim) empty at block 24047560 (plain EOA); nonce 110 at block 24025960 and 113 after block 24047560.
ground_truth_limitations: The intended recipient's full address is not published in the sources (only 0xbaf...F8b5), so it is left unset; the detector finds its own reference from the data.
Attribution as poisoning rests on public reporting plus address similarity.
